scope: 1952 Busan political crisis: cabinet resistance to dissolution, Yi Pom-sok coercion proposal, and US/UNC intervention boundary
method_note: Actor roles are separated into proposal, decision, execution, opposition and observation. FRUS reports are contemporaneous diplomatic observations, not substitutes for missing Korean signed orders. Floot untouched.

events.finding: FRUS footnote reports Rhee asked the Prime Minister to communicate a 24-hour ultimatum: pass direct-election amendment or face dissolution. No dissolution was carried out at this stage.
Chang reported most cabinet members refused to endorse dissolution; after Truman's message Rhee backed away at least temporarily.
FRUS telegram 1259 records Chang's account that Home Minister Yi proposed arresting all Assemblymen and placing them in a stockade. Treat as reported proposal, not an executed order.

events.legal_authority: Unified Command and diplomatic policy questions
events.finding: Documents show active consideration of protection, aid pressure, troop/naval signaling and even UNC martial law, but Washington and Clark repeatedly stressed exhaustion of nonmilitary means and military-resource limits.

claims.insufficient_evidence: Korean signed dissolution order not recovered; threat and legal execution must remain separate.
Source is Embassy report of Prime Minister Chang's account; Korean cabinet minutes/direct Yi statement not yet recovered.
Contingency planning existed, but documents repeatedly distinguish contingency from decision and emphasize limits/last-resort status.

adversarial_checks: Tested dissolution-threat narrative against cabinet resistance rather than assuming cabinet unanimity.
Separated Yi Pom-sok's reported proposal from an executed mass-arrest order.
Tested claim of immediate US/UNC intervention against Clark/State/Defense reluctance and resource constraints.
Preserved possibility of intervention contingency without converting planning into execution.
Separated presidential political direction from Army operational command.
Did not attribute individual legislator arrests to Rhee absent individual orders.
Did not infer Yun Woo-kyong operational responsibility solely from office title.
Did not infer Hong Pom-hi coercive acts solely from Interior vice-minister role.
Kept Chang's cabinet account marked as reported speech in a diplomatic telegram.
Kept Truman message effect temporal: Rhee backed down at least for the present, not permanently.
